subject: Materials Science
title: The History of Pottery
description: A 60-second lesson on The History of Pottery.

hook.text: The oldest known ceramic is a Venus figurine from 29,000 years ago — older than farming.

buildup.text: Early humans shaped wet clay and fired it in bonfires — the birth of ceramics.

discovery.text: Firing transforms soft clay into hard earthenware through irreversible chemical changes.

twist.text: Pottery let humans store grain and cook stews — it may have enabled permanent settlements.

climax.text: From ancient jars to modern spark plugs, ceramics remain humanity's oldest engineered material.

punchline.text: Civilization began when someone baked mud into a pot.

quiz.question: What is the oldest known ceramic artifact?
options: A Venus figurine from about 29,000 years ago
